config.explainer: In the autumn of 1755, British and New England forces seized the Acadian settlements of Nova Scotia and deported their people — the Grand Dérangement. At Grand-Pré, Lieutenant-Colonel John Winslow summoned the men and boys into the parish church on 5 September, held them prisoner, and embarked them with their families through October; his journal preserves the roll of the men held. Families were scattered from Massachusetts to Georgia, and later to Louisiana and France. A name matching this roll is the beginning of a question, not proof of descent — the same names ran through every Acadian village.
